It proposes a concrete intervention (addition of a controlled amount of carbon as an alloying element), provides a clear mechanism (formation of carbide precipitates or solid solution strengthening), and makes quantified predictions (increase in hardness by at least 15% and improvement in compressive yield strength by at least 10%). The hypothesis also specifies the material initial state, conditions, and boundary conditions, and provides a clear falsification experiment with explicit criteria. Additionally, C3 does not contain internal contradictions, mechanisms borrowed from a different alloy system without justification, or vague or hedged claims, making it the most preferable candidate.
